# 1 Samuel Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 133r–133v | **Source Image:** 1SA_003_page_001.jpg, 1SA_003_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Now the boy Samuel was ministering to the LORD in the presence of Eli. And the word of the LORD was rare in those days; there was no vision breaking forth.

**2** At that time, Eli was lying down in his usual place. His eyes had begun to grow dim, so that he could not see.

**3** The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was.

**4** Then the LORD called, "Samuel!" And he said, "Here I am."

**5** He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." But Eli said, "I did not call; go back and lie down." So he went and lay down.

**6** And the LORD called again, "Samuel!" And Samuel rose and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And he said, "I did not call, my son; go back and lie down."

**7** Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, and the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.

**8** And the LORD called Samuel a third time. He rose and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." Then Eli understood that the LORD was calling the boy.

**9** And Eli said to Samuel, "Go, lie down, and if He calls to you, say, 'Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place.

**10** And the LORD came and stood there, and called as at the other times, "Samuel! Samuel!" And Samuel said, "Speak, for Your servant is listening."

**11** And the LORD said to Samuel, "Behold, I am about to do something in Israel at which both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.

**12** On that day I will carry out against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.

**13** I have declared to him that I am judging his house forever, for the iniquity that he knew — that his sons were bringing a curse upon themselves, and he did not restrain them.

**14** Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of Eli's house shall never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering."

**15** Samuel lay down until morning, then opened the doors of the house of the LORD. And Samuel was afraid to tell Eli about the vision.

**16** Then Eli called, "Samuel, my son!" And he said, "Here I am."

**17** Eli said, "What is the word that He spoke to you? Do not hide it from me. May God deal with you severely if you hide from me anything of all that He spoke to you."

**18** So Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him. And Eli said, "He is the LORD; let Him do what is good in His eyes."

**19** And Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him, and He let none of his words fall to the ground.

**20** And all Israel, from Dan to Beer-sheba, knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.

**21** And the LORD continued to appear at Shiloh, for the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Strong agreement across all three translators on the narrative structure, verse count (21), and key theological language. The theophanic verb in v. 10 (vayyityatztzev) and Eli's submission formula in v. 18 were consistently recognized. SOPHIA follows LOGOS as baseline with targeted adjustments.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### Verse 1 — "precious" vs. "rare"
- **EMET:** "the word of YHWH was precious in those days; there was no vision breaking through"
- **LOGOS:** "the word of the LORD was precious in those days; there was no vision breaking forth"
- **PNEUMA:** "messages from the LORD were rare — visions were uncommon"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA uses "rare" — while yaqar literally means "precious/costly," its contextual meaning here is clearly about scarcity. PNEUMA captures the sense correctly. However, SOPHIA retains LOGOS's "breaking forth" over PNEUMA's "uncommon."

### Verse 7 — "know the LORD"
- **EMET:** "did not yet know YHWH"
- **LOGOS:** "did not yet know the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "had not yet come to know the LORD personally"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS. PNEUMA's "personally" is an interpretive addition — accurate but not in the Hebrew.

### Verse 13 — "bringing a curse upon themselves" vs. "blaspheming God"
- **EMET:** "bringing a curse upon themselves"
- **LOGOS:** "bringing a curse upon themselves"
- **PNEUMA:** "blaspheming God"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS with the Leningrad Codex reading. PNEUMA reconstructs a pre-tiqqun reading ("cursing God"), which is editorially legitimate but speculative. SOPHIA notes the tiqqun tradition but follows the received text.

### Verse 13 — "rebuke" vs. "restrain"
- **EMET:** "he did not rebuke them"
- **LOGOS:** "he did not rebuke them"
- **PNEUMA:** "he failed to restrain them"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA uses "restrain" — the Hebrew verb כהה in the Leningrad Codex conveys not merely verbal rebuke but active restraint. PNEUMA's reading captures the fuller sense.

### Verse 17 — oath formula
- **EMET:** "Thus may God do to you and thus may He add"
- **LOGOS:** "May God do thus to you and more also"
- **PNEUMA:** "May God deal with you severely"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows PNEUMA's concise rendering for readability while noting that EMET preserves the literal oath formula.

### Verse 19 — "let none of his words fall to the ground"
- **EMET:** "He did not let fall from all his words to the ground"
- **LOGOS:** "He let none of his words fall to the ground"
- **PNEUMA:** "He confirmed every word Samuel spoke"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS. The Hebrew idiom of words "falling to the ground" (i.e., failing to come true) is vivid and should be preserved. PNEUMA's rendering loses the image.

— SOPHIA
